title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency trading app deployed to Jerry Dunaway displayed false investment information on his screen while concealing theft of his deposits. The app used artificial intelligence to generate a fake website that showed him fictitious account balances and transaction histories, allowing the scammers to build trust through small permitted withdrawals before taking the larger sum. This is a failure of the trading platform itself, which either lacked identity verification of its operators or was designed as a fraud tool from inception.

The deployment happened entirely outside any legitimate financial institution's oversight. No human verification of the app's legitimacy, the operator's identity, or the website's authenticity occurred before Dunaway began depositing funds. It is not established whether the app was hosted on official platforms, what safeguards those platforms had in place, or how the AI-generated website was technically delivered to Dunaway's device.

The scam succeeded because Dunaway had no way to verify he was communicating with a real trading company or seeing real market data. A legitimate financial institution would have required account verification, physical identity confirmation, and regulatory licensing checks that would have blocked this fraud at the first deposit.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts of money. Unknown to Jerry, the scammers had created an artificial intelligence-generated fake website that displayed false investment information on his screen while concealing their theft.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry tried to withdraw additional funds and found he could not access his money. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway have decided to speak publicly about their experience to warn others about the sophisticated tactics scammers use. Gwinnett County police are investigating the case, but authorities say victims in these situations rarely recover their stolen funds. The couple's children have created a fundraising page to help their parents cover daily expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
